_decision: Active-path tree row labels must keep a line-height at or above the font's safe descender clearance. pathEmphasis() previously returned 'leading-none font-medium' for active-path rows, which compiled to line-height: 14px on a 14px font — a line box exactly equal to the font size. Combined with this same span's own `truncate` (overflow: hidden), Inter's descenders on g/y/p/q/j were clipped: 'Schedules' and 'System logic' lost the bottom of their letters, while rows without a descender looked fine, which is why it read as intermittent.
_why_these_four_properties: The bug is an INTERACTION between two properties, so checking either alone would pass while the defect is present. line-height 20px vs font-size 14px is the descender clearance; overflow/text-overflow/white-space confirm the truncation half is still there, since 'fix' by deleting truncate would satisfy a line-height check and silently remove the horizontal ellipsis the row also needs.
_scope: Anchored to the SELECTED leaf's label. An unselected row measures 20px whether or not the bug is present and would prove nothing — only active-path rows ever received the leading-none treatment.
